planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or nursery starts in spring in well-drained, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in bright light with some direct sun; Fukien tea has no frost tolerance and is grown outdoors year-round only in zone 10-11, elsewhere as a houseplant or patio plant brought in well before cold weather.

directions: Grow in bright light with a few hours of direct sun daily, in well-drained, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil kept evenly moist but never waterlogged. Fukien tea is a small-leaved, rough-textured evergreen shrub from Southeast Asia that is one of the most popular subjects for indoor bonsai worldwide, prized for tiny, glossy, dark green leaves, naturally gnarled and easily shaped woody stems, and a long season of small white star-shaped flowers followed by tiny red berries that can appear almost year-round in good light. It is notoriously fussy about consistency: sudden changes in light, temperature, humidity, or watering routine often trigger leaf drop, so once a good spot near a bright window is found, avoid moving the plant and keep humidity elevated with regular misting or a pebble tray. Prune and wire young growth to develop bonsai form while the plant is actively growing in spring and summer, and repot every one to two years into fresh, fast-draining mix as roots fill the container.

common_name: Serissa (Tree of a Thousand Stars, Snow Rose)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or nursery starts in spring in well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in bright light with some direct morning sun; established Serissa tolerates brief light frost outdoors in zone 8b-9, but is grown mainly as a houseplant or patio plant brought under cover before hard freezes.

directions: Grow in bright light with some direct morning sun, in well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil kept evenly moist. Serissa is a small-leaved evergreen shrub from Southeast Asia grown for its tiny, glossy, dark-green foliage and its remarkably long, nearly year-round flush of small, star-shaped white flowers (double or single depending on cultivar) that gives the plant its common name; several popular variegated cultivars offer cream-white leaf margins for added interest. Like Fukien tea, it is a classic indoor and patio bonsai subject valued for naturally fine branching and a woody, gnarled trunk that develops quickly, but it shares a reputation for dropping leaves in response to sudden changes in light, temperature, or watering, so keep conditions as consistent as possible. Prune and wire young growth in spring and summer to train bonsai shape, feed lightly during active growth, and repot every one to two years into fresh, fast-draining mix.
